text:
kendall_support: Heads up — enterprise customer reported intermittent 400s from embeddings endpoint. Error text: "embedding dimension mismatch: expected 1536 got 768". They only see it when using our Python SDK in batch mode. Can eng take a look?

 tim_eng: Do we have the exact SDK version + model name? Might be mixed-model routing like previous incidents.

 kendall_support: They supplied logs: model param = "open-embed-1536" in their call. SDK: redwood-embed==1.2.3 (python). They claim internal tenant->model mapping can flip during runtime. Repro snippet they sent (simplified):
```py
from redwood import Embeddings
client = Embeddings(model='open-embed-1536', batch_size=16)
texts = ['hi'] * 64
vecs = client.create(texts)
```
Error happens ~10% of runs, usually mid-way through processing. No precomputed vectors.

 priya_ml: Intermittent suggests either a race in client batching or a retry/resend that used different routing after mapping changed. Python SDK historically had a batch aggregation that inferred vector shape from first item. If routing changed, a later item could be handled by a different worker/model. Server-side rejects on final validation.

 vik_platform: I'll query backend logs for request IDs to see which worker and model name were used. Provide one request_id so I can correlate.

 kendall_support: Provided request_id: r-embed-77a9.

 vik_platform: Found r-embed-77a9: server saw a batch routed to model=open-embed-1536, but payload included one vector length 768. Payload source flagged as "client_precomputed" false. So client must have sent mixed-dimension content.

 tim_eng: Is it possible the client library serialized some items as precomputed vectors by accident? Like dynamic typing bug where bytes get passed through?

 essa_devex: We had a bug in python SDK <=1.2.3 where the batching layer accepted either str or list[float] per item and didn't validate types strongly when building batch matrix. Mixed inputs could produce inconsistent shapes. That was fixed in the dev branch but maybe not backported.

 priya_ml: Another vector: retries. If the SDK retries a failed batch after an auth hiccup, and the tenant->model mapping changed between attempts, the retry could be re-routed to a different model but still send the original batched payload (constructed from first attempt's shape). If model changed, dimensions mismatch.

 kendall_support: Customer also said they saw a few auth 401s right before the 400s, so that fits. They use a dynamic token rotation that can produce transient 401s.

 tim_eng: Repro plan: create a script that changes a mapping table mid-run and triggers a retry path (e.g., force a transient 502 during attempt 1). Also fuzz passing a few precomputed vectors as strings to see serialization issues. I'll run on a local staging cluster.

 essa_devex: Quick mitigation for customers: 1) Pin model explicitly in each call (pass model param per create call), 2) set batch_size=1 or small (<=4) while we patch, 3) upgrade to python-dev branch where we've added strict input validation and changed retry semantics.

 vik_platform: On server-side we can improve error text to indicate which item index had mismatched size and the expected/actual dims. That will help debug next-time. Filing an infra ticket.

 deploy-bot: Deploy queued: python-sdk/1.2.4-rc1 (patch: strict-batch-validation, retry-re-evaluate-routing) -> staging.

 priya_ml: For SDK patch we should: - validate each item is a string when model param is textual; - ensure if any item is a vector we reject the whole call unless user explicitly uses precomputed mode; - do not infer embedding dimension from first item; compute expected shape from model metadata or explicit model arg; - on retry, recompute routing and split into homogeneous batches by model.

 tim_eng: Also add an opt-in telemetry header (x-rw-embed-batch) with batch_size and sdk_version so we can correlate. Keep it opt-in for privacy.

 kendall_support: Customer tried 1.2.4-rc1 in staging and ran 50k requests with their mapping mutation enabled. No 400s so far. They still want a KB writeup describing root cause before we close.

 essa_devex: Drafted KB: "Embeddings: intermittent dimension mismatch when batching (Python SDK)". Sections: summary, root cause, short-term mitigations, recommended SDK upgrade, example safe usage. Will paste sample code.

 priya_ml: Suggested safe code sample to include in KB:
```py
# explicit per-call model pin + small batch
from redwood import Embeddings
emb = Embeddings(batch_size=4, timeout=45)
# pass model explicitly to avoid runtime routing ambiguity
vecs = emb.create(["Hello","World"], model='open-embed-1536')
```

# node example for customers using TS SDK
```ts
import { Embeddings } from 'redwood';
const emb = new Embeddings({ batchSize: 8 });
await emb.create(["a","b","c"], { model: 'open-embed-1536' });
```

 vik_platform: After we ship stable 1.2.4, I'll backfill server-side error text and add a monitoring alert for mixed-dimension failures to catch regressions.

 kendall_support: Customer confirmed they will move to 1.2.4 stable and pin models. I'll keep case open until they confirm in 7 days.

 tim_eng: Action items: ENG-2320 (SDK strict validation + retry semantics), INF-874 (improved server error reporting), DOC-459 (KB article). Linking support case SC-10234.

 essa_devex: Added unit tests to python SDK to ensure batching rejects mixed content and that retry re-evaluates per-item routing. Will land today.

 kendall_support: Thanks everyone. Will update customer and close after final confirmation. :thumbsup:
